Can you swim at Bang Por Beach? | Yes, but only around high tide and in calm conditions. At low tide the sea retreats 50 m or more over a flat of sand, mud and stones, so it becomes a place to walk, not swim. Wear reef shoes and check our tide card before you go.
Why do reviews of Bang Por disagree so much? | Because the tide changes the beach completely. At high tide it is calm water over sand that suits a swim; at low tide it is a wide, stony and muddy flat where people collect shellfish. Both descriptions are true at different times of day.
Is Bang Por good for seafood? | Yes, it is one of the best areas on Samui for seafood by the sea. Restaurants along the ring road grill fish, prawns, squid and crab priced by weight, and Bang Por Seafood (Takho) is listed in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, open daily 10:00–22:00.
Can you watch the sunset at Bang Por? | Yes. The bay faces north-west, so the sun goes down towards the Laem Yai headland and the sea, and in the winter months, when it sets further south behind the land, the sky still colours over the bay. Sunset falls between about 17:55 and 18:45 depending on the month.
Is Bang Por calm in the rainy season? | Usually calmer than the east coast. The north-west coast is in the lee of the island during the October–December north-east monsoon, so it rarely gets the surf and red flags of Chaweng and Lamai, though it still gets heavy rain, especially in November.
Do your tours pick up from Bang Por? | Yes. Hotel pickup is included from most areas of Koh Samui; Bang Por sits on the edge of the standard area, and towards Nathon and the west coast a supplement of 400 THB per person return applies. Send us your address on WhatsApp and we'll confirm before you book.
How far is Bang Por from the airport? | About 22 km, or 30–40 minutes by car along the ring road. Airport taxis charge by zone; expect roughly 500–700 THB, and note that Grab coverage on the west side is thin in the evening.
